LVKE.|165}}</noinclude>generation, how long shal I be vvith you and suffer you? bring hither thy sonne. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=42}}† And vvhen he came to him, the deuil dashed, and tore him. And {{sc|Iesvs}} rebuked the vncleane spirit, and healed the lad: and rendred him to his father. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=43}}† And al vvere astonied at the might of God: and al merueiling at al things that he did, he said to his disciples, {{verse|chapter=9|verse=44}}† Lay you in your hartes these vvordes, for it shal come to passe that the Sonne of man shal be deliuered into the hands of men. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=45}}† But they did not know this vvord, and it vvas couered before them, that they perceiued it not. And they vvere afraid to aske him of this vvord.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=46}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 18, 1. Mar. 9, 34.''}}* And there entred {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Desire of preeminence is an humane infirmitie often euen among the good. Against which, Christ teacheth humility, but forbiddeth not Superiority.}}∷ a cogitation into them, vvhich of them should be greater. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=47}}† But {{sc|Iesvs}} seeing the cogitations of their hart, tooke a childe and set him by him, {{verse|chapter=9|verse=48}}† and said to them, Whosoeuer receiueth this childe in my name, receiueth me: and vvhosoeuer receiueth me, receiueth him that sent me. For he that is the lesser among you al, he is the greater.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=49}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 9, 38.''}}* And Iohn ansvvering said, Maister, vve savv a certaine man casting out deuils in thy name, and vve prohibited him, because he folovveth not vvith vs. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=50}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ There be some that folow not Christ precisely in life and doctrine, of whom vve may make our aduantage to the propagation of Christes honour and religion, when they doe any thing for the aduancement thereof, of vvhat intention soeuer they doe it. ''Philip. 1, 15''.}}∷ Prohibit not. for he that is not against you, is for you.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=51}}† And it came to passe, vvhiles the daies of his assumption vvere accomplishing, and he fixed his face to goe into Hierusalem. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=52}}† And he sent messengers before his face: and going they entred into a citie of the Samaritans to prepare for him. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=53}}† And they receiued him not, because his {{sup|‖}} face vvas to goe to Hierusalem. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=54}}† And vvhen his disciples Iames and Iohn had seen it, they said, Lord vvilt thou vve say that fire come dovvne from heauen and consume {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`them as Elias also did''?}}`them'? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=55}}† And turning, {{sup|‖}} he rebuked them, saying, You knovv not of vvhat spirit you are. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=56}}† The sonne of man came not to destroy soules, but to saue.

And they vvent into an other tovvne. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=57}}† And it came to passe as they vvalked in the vvay, a certaine man said to him, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 8, 19.''}}* I vvil folovv thee vvhithersoeuer thou goest. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=58}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ This man would haue folowed him for temporal commodities, and therfore was not suffered.}}∷ The foxes haue holes, and the foules of the aire nestes: but the sonne of man hath not where to repose his head. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=59}}† But he said to an other, Folow me. And he said, Lord, permit me first to goe, and to burie my father. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=60}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, Let the dead burie their dead: but goe thou, set forth the kingdom of God. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=61}}† And an other said, I vvil folovv thee Lord, but permit me<noinclude>{{rh||X iij|first}}</noinclude>
